- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.2) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp upward spikes in price; cap forecast at +10% above recent peak if sentiment is bullish.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days above 68.00 then drops), model tends to lag; anticipate downward correction in next 3–5 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often misses the “late-cycle” peak (last 5–7 days of true outcome); shift forecast horizon to align with 28–30 day true trend.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., 0.8 → 0.0 → 0.8), model misreads momentum; use sentiment-weighted smoothing to dampen false momentum signals.
